objective: Turn the owner console into a calm operator cockpit with immediate live people awareness, task-based controls, and explicit security boundaries.

series.outcome: Start scripts open the operator console while the employee kiosk remains a separate shared-device route.
acceptance: Operator header communicates runtime state without a marketing-style hero

series.outcome: The owner token validates once, clears from the visible field, and remains only in tab memory until lock or reset.
acceptance: Enter and Unlock share the same validation path
Invalid tokens clear from the field
Lock session closes the owner WebSocket and removes the in-memory token

series.outcome: Employee and guest WebSocket information appears near the top with polling fallback and owner clock-out actions.
acceptance: Employee and guest counts are visible above task controls
Roster filters support all, employee, and guest views
Owner actions refresh the live roster without a page reload

series.outcome: Dense owner controls are separated into Today, Employees, Payroll, Guests, Recovery, Readiness, and Security tasks.
acceptance: Only the selected task cards are visible
Security setup automatically opens when no owner token is configured

series.outcome: Operators can generate, copy, and open a LAN-aware employee kiosk QR/link.
acceptance: Generate Employee QR refreshes the preferred LAN URL
PIN remains required after QR launch

series.outcome: Apply the salvage cockpit visual language with compact hierarchy, accessible states, responsive layout, and reduced card noise.
acceptance: Desktop and mobile layouts remain readable
Hidden task panels do not remain focusable
No owner secret is persisted in localStorage or sessionStorage
Browser flow tests cover unlock, task switching, QR generation, and session lock

source_of_truth_rules.live_transport: authenticated WebSocket with 15-second HTTP polling fallback

non_claims: The generated QR is a local-network convenience, not an authentication credential.
